doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Wishing for a million dollars to quit or buy a club
summary: If she had a million dollars she would play only gigs she wanted or buy a club, and notes Artie Shaw quit while Lionel Hampton works while old.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Thank you. I’d like to ask you another question. What are your hopes and wishes now?
I hope I get a million dollars, then I’ll quit the business.
Is that true? You would really quit the business?
Yes, the business ain’t what it’s cracked up to be.
If you had the million dollars, what would you do instead of playing?
I would play occasionally. I’d take gigs that I wanted, not gigs somebody else wanted me to do.
I think that sounds good to me, too. Because you come to such a point, don’t you?
Yeah, it’s time to quit. Lena, it’s time to quit. Sit down before you fall down.
So, you’ve played, you think, almost every place you wanted to and if you had a million dollars would you think of building your own self a club and playing in it?
Maybe I’d buy a club that’s already put up.
And then play when you get ready.
When I get ready. I call the shots.
I like that. I think that’s a very, very good way….
Like Artie Shaw, he quit. He took that clarinet and they said, broke it across a mirror.
Is that true? Artie Shaw.
When most of us, we played when we sick. Like Lionel Hampton, 80 years old, should be not working.
I think that’s keeping him alive, don’t you?
No, that’s keeping him tired. And somebody said, his manager stole his money.
Maybe that’s why he has to work.
Could be.
